q-131540.name: Question 1
q-131540.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(X<x)=P(Z<\frac{x-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-4$ and $\sigma =1.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<-4.47) & =P(Z<\frac{-4.47-(-4)}{1}) \\  & =P(Z<-0.47) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.47) \\  & =Φ(-0.47)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/b7855674356d8fad68f144d19bacd47d1818b3bb05a8d466bb6aec645e769bf3.png)

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(-0.47)=0.3192.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(X<-4.47)=0.3192.
$$

q-335886.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $Y∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(Y\ge y)=P(Z\ge \frac{y-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-2$ and $\sigma =4.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge -4.48) & =P(Z\ge \frac{-4.48-(-2)}{4}) \\  & =P(Z\ge -0.62).\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/2547a2e847c503d8cdf6c2df258edd7c51e1478185f2cb0055f72425ed6fd04e.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -0.62) & =1-P(Z<-0.62) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -0.62) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.62).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(-0.62)=0.2676.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -0.62) & =1-Φ(-0.62) \\  & =1-0.2676 \\  & =0.7324.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(Y\ge -4.48)=0.7324.
$$
